children: An expert panel of the EU drug regulator, the European Medicines Agency, endorsed 12 new medicines and 11 label expansions for approval this week, benefiting drugmakers including Merck
, AstraZeneca
, Roche
, and Corcept Therapeutics
Merck

The New Jersey-based pharma giant announced on Friday that EMA’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use issued a positive opinion on a combination regimen containing its anti-PD-1 therapy Keytruda for bladder cancer.
Specifically, the CHMP has endorsed Keytruda and its injectable version, Keytruda SC, for use with Pfizer’s
antibody-drug conjugate, Padcev, as neoadjuvant therapy (before surgery) and then as adjuvant therapy (after cystectomy) for adults with resectable muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

The European Commission will next review the recommendation before finalizing the label expansion, potentially by Q4 2026, a decision applicable in the European Union as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, and
AstraZeneca
The Anglo-Swedish drugmaker received a positive CHMP opinion for a label expansion of its antibody-drug conjugate Enhertu, marketed with Daiichi Sankyo
as a late-line option for certain cases of breast cancer.

The committee endorsed Enhertu as an adjuvant therapy for adults with resected HER2-positive breast cancer who have residual invasive disease following neoadjuvant taxane-based and HER2-targeted treatment, Astra
said.
Roche

CHMP issued a positive opinion on the Swiss drugmaker’s Ocrevus for children aged 10 years and older with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune condition affecting the central nervous system. The antibody therapy is already available in the region for adults with relapsing forms of MS and primary progressive MS. A final decision on the label expansion is expected from the EC in the near future, according to Roche
Corcept
Corcept Therapeutics’

ovarian cancer therapy relacorilant was among the new medicines to receive a positive CHMP opinion this week. The committee recommended marketing authorization for the drug branded as Lifyorli in the U.S. for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in combination with the chemotherapy drug nab-paclitaxel. The EC is expected to review the CHMP view before issuing a final decision
Zealand Pharma
The Danish drugmaker
received a positive CHMP opinion on its GLP-2 analog, Zeydovio (glepaglutide), for the treatment of adults with short bowel syndrome, a rare disease characterized by impaired intestinal function.
